item.title: AI Pair Programming ROI 2026: Real Productivity Metrics from Dev Teams
item.description: 85% of developers now use at least one AI tool in their daily workflow, and 22% of all merged code across a 135,000-developer dataset is AI-authored. Those numbers sound like a productivity revolution. The reality is messier. Some controlled experiments show developers completing tasks 19% slower with AI assistance, even while believing they are 24% faster. Meanwhile, enterprises running disciplined AI programs report 4:1 returns — $150 in developer time saved for every $37.50 spent on AI tooling per incremental pull request. The gap between those outcomes is not about which tool you picked. It is about how you measure, deploy, and constrain the tool. This guide works through the actual data — the good numbers, the uncomfortable numbers, and the calculation framework your team can run today to find out which bucket you are in.
